answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation employer-staked: an identity earns standing only when a real principal locks tokens behind its work, like pigment bonded into cedar wood rather than a coat of paint. If the agent cheats, the stake is slashed, so the principal loses money too. A whisper campaign of fake identities fails because each clone needs a distinct sponsor willing to risk capital, and sponsors who back junk lose their stake, so the attacker's cost scales with every identity while honest agents accumulate backing cheaply.
